items.d: Displays automobiles from various eras from 1880s to 1970s. It also has over 100 bicycles from historical to present day.
A beach at Luzanovka neighborhood, easily reachable by numerous bus routes which link the city centre with the Poselok Kotovskogo section of Odesa.
The former quarry nearby transformed into a museum. During weekends from spring to fall, the narrow-gauge railway is also in operation, along with small buffet in a tram.
Here you can see yachts.
A Friday Mosque dating from the 18th and 19th centuries for up to 1,500 people
Relates the story of the armed conflict of the 1980s-90s in El Salvador and the heartbreak of lives lost during it.
Forbidden to enter on premises but you can peek the buildings from the entrance gate.
Former parliamentary building. Still in use for seminars.
The Old Town Hall and Apponyi Palace is open to the public as a museum, with an exhibition of city history.
Eielson Visitor Center is open in summer only and provides one of the most dramatic views of the mountain, if you are lucky enough to visit on a day when it isn't shrouded in clouds.

in.fr: parc national et réserve du Denali

items.d: With a capacity of 20,000, this is home to Knights team, representing Free State province.
This is a common tour stop, often shrugged at by those who go there. However, if you take a tour bus there, to get a laugh you can always tell people that you took the bus to Hell.
An Orthodox church built from 179 –1795. Stephan the Great monument is just across the street.
This interesting museum of local history has been rehabilitated and should not be missed. Abu Abdullo Rudaki was a famous poet of the 10th century.

n.en: Rudaki Museum (Republican History and Regional Study Museum)

items.d: Kočo Racin was an author and partisan who is considered a founder of modern Macedonian literature. He was born to a poor family in Veles in 1908 and he died at just 34 years of age in what is believed by some to have been a…
A 575-m-high mountain whose name means the anvil in Spanish, about 30 min by bici-taxi from the centre of town. A return normal taxi is about CUC15.
Runs a consistently avant-garde set of exhibits, with no permanent collection. In it's usual location has an excellent café, Nikau, attached to it.
The original museum from 1924 was part of the mosque complex; it moved here in 1971 as the collection expanded. The museum displays the area's eventful history, majoring on the Thracian period.

The spa and sauna center features a swimming pool, cold water pool and Japanese pool, small children’s pool, jacuzzi and foot baths, 2 steam baths, juniper sauna, Finnish sauna, birch sauna, aroma sauna, salt room, Garra Rufa…
Houses a priceless collection of Rhodesiana and Africana in the form of diaries, notebooks and reports of various origins.
An abandoned fishing village, founded in the early 17th century and fully abandoned in the 1970s with the shift of Qatar's economy to one based on mineral resources.
If you have never seen a big snake or python, this one looks quite nice. Otherwise the trip (the monastery is a bit off the track) is not worth it.
Closed for renovation until 2026A great museum on the history of Northern Ostrobothnia, especially the history of Oulu. Exhibitions on four floors.
Transport museum with various old trams and buses on display.
Services include Beginner Kitesurf Lessons, Kiteboarding Rental, IKO Instructor Training Course and Advanced private lessons with Profesional IKO Kiteboard Instructors to improve your level.
Established in 1989, this national museum has four exhibit rooms devoted to the preservation of Comoros' cultural heritage.
Next to the Panteon Nacional. One of the best hidden gems of Caracas. A private collection of Boulton's family.

Set in a colonial building, this museum contains artifacts significant to Pilar, including when it was the Casa de Gobierno (house of government) while Pilar was the provisional capital during the Triple Alliance War.

Spanish language school that offers group, private, surf and special courses such as the "crash course" for travellers (1 to 5 days). The school also offers cultural activities and excursions during the week to practice Spanish.
Reopened in mid-2013 after complete renovation. Fewer than 200 animals from more than 100 species. Nice lion exhibit.
Built in 2016, the Peace Park is the most popular park in the city with over 700 people coming to visit, take pictures and just enjoy the green every day.
A park with 23 waterslides, a 350-m wave river, a wave pool, a range of other pools, and a disco. Food is overpriced and they search you to keep it that way.

From Qazvin you can do a day trip to the mountains of Alborz. Most visitors go here to see the remains of Hasan-e-Sabah's castle Alamut, from where he ruled the assassins order, a medieval terrorist organisation.
In parkland south of the main square is this yellow clock tower. Several of the defunct railway tunnels can be viewed from nearby.
Rental of snowboards, cross-country skis, snow scooters and other winter sports equipment. Friendly and efficient owner who can provide information on snow and ice conditions.
Our Lady of Baluarte from 1522 is one of the oldest European structures in the Southern Hemisphere.

n.en: Chapel of Nossa Senhora de Baluarte

items.d: "The Rebel Army" were relegated in 2025 - they're a yo-yo team and now play soccer in League of Ireland First Division, the second tier. The playing season is Feb–Nov and matches are usually on Friday evenings.

The official residence of the governor-general was built as two separate houses in the 17th century. In 1801, Lord Lavington of Carlisle acquired the house. Renovations are expected to be completed Jan 2026.
More relaxing and a bit more discreet than either Baldi & Tabacon. Reservations definitely recommended as they limit to 100 guests. Good dinner and drinks.
